subject: Hosted API minimum commit, on-demand fallback & surge credits — proposal
messages:
From: Laura Keane <laura.keane@clipperlogistics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clipperlogistics.com; devops@clipperlogistics.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify minimum spend / overage for hosted API (follow-up)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Before we move to procurement, a couple of commercial clarifications from our side so we can budget and prepare change requests:

- Minimum monthly spend: would Clipper be required to commit to a minimum monthly $ amount for hosted API? If so, can you confirm the minimum and whether unused commit rolls over or converts to credits?
- On-demand fallback / overage: if we exceed committed tokens in a month, what is the on-demand rate (per-token) and how is it billed? Is there a different "burst" surcharge for spikes vs continuous overage?
- First-time surge cushion: for new customers, do you offer any grace on the first large unexpected burst (e.g., first 10% over commit) before applying higher overage multipliers?

Procurement wants to see these spelled out so we can compare against other vendors. Do you have a short doc or table we can include in the SOW?

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Keane
Head of Platform, Clipper Logistics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Keane <laura.keane@clipperlogistics.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com; ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify minimum spend / overage for hosted API (follow-up)

Hi Laura —

Appreciate the clear list. I pulled together a concise proposal and attached a simple pricing tiers sheet (Redwood_Pricing_Tiers_v3.xlsx). Key points up front:

- Minimum monthly commit: $15,000/month for the hosted API product (three-month ramp allowed). Unused committed spend converts to account credit for the following quarter (no cash refunds).
- Overage/on-demand: billed at 1.9x the per-token list rate when continuous overage (more than 20% above commit for >5 consecutive days in billing month).
- Burst surcharge (spikes): single-day or short spikes (<=48 hours) above commit billed at 1.25x list rate, with the first 10% aggregated monthly overage waived as a one-time onboarding cushion (applies only in the first billing month after go-live).

Questions for you to confirm so we can finalize the SOW:
1) Do you need rollover credits to apply monthly or quarterly?
2) Is Clipper willing to commit to a 12-month term in exchange for a 10% committed volume discount?

I've looped in Soojin (pricing/product) and Ben (sales lead) for any finer tweaks or legal/SLAs. If that looks directionally ok I can put a short paragraph into the proposal PDF and send for DocuSign.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if easier.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Tiers_v3.xlsx

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Keane <laura.keane@clipperlogistics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify minimum spend / overage for hosted API (follow-up)

Laura, Marcus — quick pricing note from product/ops side to make the mechanics clear:

- Rollover: unused commit converts to a quarter-window credit (applies to the following quarter only). Credits are applied before any overage is billed.
- Overage bands:
  - Spike band (<=48h): 1.25x list per-token
  - Short sustained (48h–5d): 1.45x list per-token
  - Continuous (>=5d and >20% over commit average): 1.9x list per-token and may trigger automatic scaling guidance to dedicated capacity.
- Onboarding cushion: first billing month includes a one-time 10% cushion (calculated against committed tokens) that we do not charge for.
- True-up mechanics: we bill monthly and include a true-up invoice; any dispute window is 30 days.

Operational note for SREs (Sam copy to procurement/devops): we can add an option to enable an automated soft-fallback policy that routes excess traffic to a slightly cheaper compatible model when on-demand rates exceed a threshold you define. That can materially lower your overage cost during known spike windows.

If Clipper wants to lock a lower overage multiplier for the term, we can include a graduated discount tied to a 12/24-month commit — Marcus can propose the bands.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Pricing & Product Operations, Redwood
